newsitem.title: USA: Reuter Mfg retires debt, sees Q2 gain.
newsitem.headline: Reuter Mfg retires debt, sees Q2 gain.

text.p: Reuter Manufacturing Inc said Tuesday it exchanged $3,750,000 of cash for two debt instruments held by Sanwa Business Credit Corp, effective March 31, 1997.

The instruments settled in the exchange represented obligations carried over from previous financing associated with discontinued waste operations and had an aggregate carrying value of about $6.9 million. The company said the exchange will result in in an extraordinary gain in its second quarter ending June 30 of about $3.5 million.
In addition, Reuter Manufacturing owed Sanwa about $252,500 under the two instruments for the first quarter of 1997. That amount was paid concurrently with the exchange.
A warrant to Sanwa for 3,178,780 shares of common stock and a trading standstill agreement with certain directors also were terminated with the transaction.

The company said $4.552,000 was raised by a successful private placement of 1,517,333 shares of common stock at $3 per share. The excess of the cash raised over the foregoing payments to Sanwa was applied to the expenses of the private placement and to general company funds.
In addition to related commissions, a five-year warrant for 50,000 shares of common stock was issued for a nominal payment to John G. Kinnard and Co, which helped with the private placement.
Reuter Manufacturing makes and assembles medical products and other parts on a contract basis.
